notLaunchableReason: hafleet-up creates a tmux session and an ACP agent has no pane; start it with `hafleet acp-up <name> <workspace> octos` instead

launch.permissionSummary: octos sandbox as configured (hafleet never passes --danger-full-access)
launch.acpArgsNote: coding-full is required, not a preference. octos's default 'coding' profile narrows the tool registry with ToolRegistry::filter_by_profile, an allow-list retain(). MCP tool names are not in that list, so operator-configured MCP tools are evicted — and because McpService is an Arc<RunningService>, eviction drops the last references and cancels the transport. Observed on mini5 as 'MCP server started tools=11' followed 1ms later by 'task cancelled' and 'Child exited'. Under coding-full the child survives and the agent reaches HAFleet's tools: verified by octos calling whoami and check_inbox and returning their real output.
launch.acpCwdFlagNote: octos acp accepts --cwd as the default working directory when a client omits it from session/new. hermes-acp rejects the flag and dies before the handshake, so it is declared per adapter rather than assumed.
launch.acpModelFlagNote: Verified: `octos acp --help` lists --model <MODEL> and the handshake survives it. Declared separately from launch.modelFlag because that one describes the tmux CLI, and the two are not the same surface — hermes-acp and codex-acp take no model flag at all even though their CLIs do.

flags.comment: octos treats full access as a per-run opt-in it refuses to even persist — config_layer.rs: 'full access is a per-run opt-in, not a saved default that would silently disable the sandbox'. A hafleet-launched agent runs detached, takes instructions from the message API, and has nobody watching, so it must not be able to widen its own sandbox.
flags.message: Octos sandbox flag is managed by hafleet: {token}

signals.comment: ACP reports progress as session/update notifications, so there is no pane to scrape and no readiness marker to match. These stay empty on purpose; they exist for tmux-driven frameworks.

acp.comment: Verified against octos 2.0.2 on a real host: initialize -> session/new -> session/prompt returned stopReason end_turn, with the reply streamed back as agent_message_chunk updates.
acp.blocksOnPermissionRequestNote: octos surfaces tool calls as ACP tool_call records but does not block on session/request_permission in v1, so hafleet can observe permission activity and cannot answer it. The sandbox chosen at launch remains the real control.
acp.mcpServersNote: octos ignores mcpServers on ACP session/new (acp.rs: 'ignored in v1'). HAFleet's tools must instead be declared in octos's own config at ~/.config/octos/config.json under mcp_servers, which the ACP session loader does honour (acp.rs:431). HAFleet does not write that file; see docs.
